newsitem.title: UK: UK govt - About 60 mln stg pension compensation paid.
newsitem.headline: UK govt - About 60 mln stg pension compensation paid.

text.p: About 60 million pounds in compensation has been paid out so far to British people who were mis-sold pensions, Economic Secretary to the Treasury Angela Knight said on Monday.

Figures from the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) showed "about 60 million pounds of compensation had been made in the period up to December 31, 1996," Knight said in a written response to a parliamentary question.

The PIA regulates the sale of investment products to the public. Pension mis-selling has affected several hundred thousand people who may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions by financial companies during the late 1980s and early 1990s.
Earlier this year, industry sources said the PIA was holding a series of meetings with firms with a large number of cases yet to be settled to get them to outline their plans to clear up the backlog.

In response to further questions, Knight said it was not possible to list the companies which have mis-sold personal pensions nor to give a reliable estimate of the number of people who were sold inappropriate policies.
